tagline: Down the Iowa River from the Meskwaki to the Amanas.
intro: The byway runs 77 miles down the Iowa River valley, through farmland and river wetlands, from the edge of the Meskwaki Settlement west of Tama east to the Amana Colonies. The Czech Trail towns of Clutier, Vining, Elberon and Chelsea sit in country the locals call the Bohemian Alps, and northwest of Chelsea an observation deck is built in the shape of an eagle in flight.
The Meskwaki bought this ground back themselves in 1857, a small piece of what they had lost by treaty in 1842. It is Iowa's only resident Native American community.

moments.title: Lincoln Highway Bridge, Tama
moments.text: A short 1914 bridge carries the old Lincoln Highway over Mud Creek with the road's name spelled out in its concrete railings, paid for by local boosters.

moments.title: Preston's Station, Belle Plaine
moments.text: George Preston bought the gas station in 1923 for $100, it pumped gas until 1989, and antique advertising and highway signs now cover it and the garage beside it.

moments.title: Amana Colonies
moments.text: German Pietists kept a communal life in these seven villages until 1932, and in July thousands of American lotus bloom on Lily Lake at Amana.
